Map the data.
Verify the ledger.

1. Start with the included fixture

The repository contains a two-item order paid in two captures, followed by a partial refund. Run the commands in the README. Expected contribution is ₹72.60, then ₹52.60 after the refund grant, then ₹42.60 after additional advertising. Returning refund cash changes the reconciliation balance, not revenue a second time.

2. Map your store export to five tables

Orders: stable order/customer IDs, sale date, channel, shipping cost and INR currency. Line items: line and order IDs, product, quantity, unit price, line discount and historical unit cost. Payments: immutable capture/refund event ID, order, date, terminal success/failure, amount and actual fee. Refunds: refund grant ID, original line, date and amount. Spend: stable cost event ID, date, channel and amount.

All money is integer paise. Input fields are named and validated. An order and at least one initial line arrive together; your mapper must verify completeness. Additional distinct lines can arrive later. Payments and refund events may follow later. Use the store's timezone consistently. Do not substitute missing costs with zero.

3. Reconcile before relying on it

Check source row counts, currencies, totals and date coverage. Review quarantined batches and collection/refund liabilities. Replay the same export: no extra source rows or financial effects should appear. Compare incremental output against a full refresh before using the figures for decisions.

What needs an adapter

Platform-specific API pagination, authentication, rate limits, cancelled/draft order filtering, discount/tax mapping, source updates, refund allocation and secret storage. None is implemented for Shopify, WooCommerce or another platform yet. This is a working canonical batch contract, not a universal plug-and-play connector.

Supported boundaries

Single store per database, INR only, immutable accepted sales/events, single writer, local scheduled or manual batch use. No tax, shipping income, chargebacks, restocking, cost corrections, partial cancellations, FX, server deployment or real-time ingestion. Do not force unsupported events into the nearest field.
